title.narrative: Improved labour administration, labour inspection, social dialogue, and collective bargaining that enhance working conditions, including wages, across various forms of employment

description.narrative: Mongolia faces a range of labour market challenges, including a shortage of labour force due to demographic change and transition, labour market mismatch and skills gap and high informal employment. To address those challenges, the labour administration needs to improve its governance and enforcement, through strengthened labour inspection capacity and improved policy coordination capacity. Quality of labour administration and well-functioning industrial relations can help to improve labour market governance, adequate protection of labour rights and the ability of institutions effectively respond to economic and social changes. A comparatively well-established legal system (Labour law of 2021, Social Insurance Package Law of 2023 and upcoming OSH law and Employment Promotion Law) and the tripartite mechanism and social dialogue at the national level are becoming the main opportunity for Mongolia further address the challenges mentioned above. Expected results: 1) Improved effectiveness, coverage, and quality of labour inspection in the services sector, leading to better compliance with labour standards, safer workplaces, and strengthened protection of workersâ€™ rights; 2) The Office will support Mongoliaâ€™s tripartite constituents by strengthening social dialogue and enhancing collective bargaining at both sectoral and enterprise levels through the development of practical handbooks and guidelines for employers and workers, alongside piloted training sessions in selected enterprises where the ILO is currently providing support to improve workplace cooperation.
